title: Taiwan digital affairs ministry official urges firms to notify early and recover fast as AI speeds attacks
date_note: Forum remarks were made on 24 November per the article; the article was published 25 November.
summary: Cheng Wei, head of the information and communications security department at Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs, told a Digital Trust Forum on 24 November that companies should not wait until they finish investigating a breach before notifying customers and partners. He said AI has reduced the cost of cyberattacks and increased their speed. As of 11 November, about 10 companies and online platforms had been attacked, per the article.
plain: A Taiwanese digital affairs ministry official told a forum that companies should warn customers and partners early about a breach, without waiting for the investigation to end, because AI has made attacks cheaper and faster.
exec: Taiwan's digital affairs ministry official says firms should not delay breach notices, and that AI has made attacks cheaper and faster.
action: As the ministry official advises, notify customers and partners of a breach without waiting for the investigation to finish.
geo_basis: Ministry of Digital Affairs, Taiwan, as stated by the article; city not stated, capital used

evidence.quote: Companies should not wait until they finish investigating a breach incident.
As of November 11, about 10 companies and online platforms had been attacked.

validation.note: One publisher (Digital Today) relaying IT Home's report of the forum remarks; no ministry page was read.
